title: Land Abandonment and Climate Warming Drove Two Centuries of Natural Forest Expansion in the Alps
content:
Using two centuries of harmonized land-cover data across the European Alps, we show forest cover increased by ~25%, peaking mid-20th century driven by land abandonment. Since the 1980s, expansion has slowed, become spatially diffuse, and shifted toward the treeline, possibly reflecting climate warming's growing influence.


ABSTRACT

Natural forest expansion (NFE) is a widespread consequence of land abandonment and climate change in mountain systems, yet its long-term spatiotemporal patterns and the relative influence of land-use and climate change remain poorly resolved. Here we compile and analyse a harmonized dataset of forest cover derived from historical maps and aerial/satellite imagery to assess NFE across the European Alps over the past 200 years. Using machine learning and spatial statistical models, we quantified spatiotemporal changes and analysed the trade-offs between drivers of NFE over time. NFE in the region was quantified in 1.55 million ha since the early 19th century (16% of the European Alps), with a peak between the end of World War II and the 1980s (11,260 ha year−1), largely driven by widespread land abandonment. Although conservation efforts intensified during this period, protected areas were typically designated in high-elevation and remote areas already undergoing forest transitions, suggesting they followed rather than initiated change. Over the last four decades, the pace of NFE has slowed (7195 ha year−1), spatial clustering has weakened, and forest gains have increasingly shifted toward treeline ecotones. Together, our results indicate a system in transition, with a temporal reorganization of forest expansion from land-use legacies and gap filling toward stronger environmental constraints at higher elevations. These findings provide a long-term perspective on how interacting socio-economic and climatic drivers shape forest transitions in mountain regions under ongoing global change.
